reviews.title: Not working for me at first…
reviews.text: I’ve had the Timepage app for several years. I added Actions a couple of years ago. Always loved the look of the app, but, it felt counterintuitive, so I kept going back to Reminders. Well, either I changed or an update changed how we enter and edit actions. In any case, it works really well now and I’m happy using it with Timepage. Thanks.

I'm going to have to cancel my subscription having wasted most of the annual cost for the app bundle by the time it expires.

reviews.title: Flaky

reviews.title: Cannot use without two-way sync with Reminders
reviews.text:
I love the Moleskine productivity suite. I LOVE it passionately; it’s beautiful, intuitive, and dynamic, but I cannot use this set of apps for exactly one reason: I need a two-way sync with Apple Reminders. It is non-negotiable. I canceled my last subscription because of it and was very disappointed to see it has still not been implemented. I love this set of apps, but it is literally completely unusable to me because of this one flaw. 

Without this two-way sync, I cannot assign tasks to other people or share tasks/lists with other people, nor can I track other people’s progress on tasks. I can’t use Apple Reminder triggers that aren’t available in Moleskine. I can’t easily move a task from one platform to another. It’s such a shame. I love this set of apps, and it’s amazing to me that despite the consistent and unrelenting feedback from end users about the need for this two-way sync, Moleskine chooses to continue biting the hands that feed.

Haven’t had the subscription for a while because I tried to lean on Apple Reminders. @Bonobo, Will Actions ever support tags and smart lists? I don’t want to add a GoodTask subscription to my productivity expenses but I’d buy back into Actions and Timepage if tags and smart lists are ever introduced. Smart list filtering would have to be more robust than Apple Reminders, though. Like include or exclude on multiple criteria.

reviews.title: Love the Timepage and Actions

My only feedback is that it would be great to add notes to subscribed calendars, as currently there’s no way to interact with them beyond viewing.

reviews.title: Needs a few updates to make things more clear
reviews.text: The search bar is completely annoying when I search for a note and it floats up and down across the screen using the graphic layout elements. It’s really silly.  My other main grade is after creating a note. There is a button at the bottom and you have to click “done”. This is fairly similar to the button that you click to mark a task completed with a checkmark.  It needs to be clear when you are finished creating a task versus when you have actually completed the task. The button needs to look a lot different than a checkmark and maybe the Dunn button needs to look a lot different. It’s just confusing. All in all a clean app but really needs to be a little more clear for quick use while on the road.

reviews.title: Decent overall
reviews.text:
Pros
1. Pretty easy to organize with how the app allows you to structure tasks into different lists
2. Good ability to manipulate the ordering of tasks with dragging to position. 
3. Easy to apply details such as time, repetition, notes, reminders to tasks
2. Display is simple and easy to understand. 

Cons - just some extra steps that could be eliminated for increasing the simplicity of using the app. The cons are not bad enough to not buy the app. 
1. When adding new tasks the order is displayed as last task created to first. So if you wanted to add tasks in order of completion, it will display them backwards. This requires additional steps of dragging tasks to their proper place in the sequence. 
2. If you want a task to have a time written before the name of the task (4pm Dr. appointment), the app will automatically assign the time to the reminder part and remove it from the name. So you will have to create the task, save it, go out, open it, and then type in the time in the name, and then save.

reviews.title: Almost great but ultimately, it’s Aggravating
reviews.text:
Let’s start with what’s so aggravating about this app:

If you hit the Trashcan icon your item/changes disappear. Makes sense. (No Are you sure? though)

If you hit the Checkmark your item/changes disappear.

If you hit the button that makes your iPad keyboard go down your changes disappear. 

If you make changes to an item then tap outside the box, box goes away…unchanged

The ONLY way to hold on to this stuff and not have to re-do the work is to click the little word “done” at the top of your keyboard. WHY? I got this app because I’m a visual thinker and I just can’t get used to this. 

I’ve had Actions for years, it could be great. I love that you can organized tasks visually, drag and drop them onto days. If it weren’t for these aggravations I think I would be in the app every day and it could really help me stay organized. but it’s still not intuitive for me so I’ve cancelled my subscription.

reviews.title: Logbook doesn’t work anymore, which seriously hurts usability
reviews.text: I used to swear by this app, but I’ve noticed that after the last couple of updates the logbook doesn’t work anymore. I checked my settings to see if maybe I needed to opt in, but I can see that my “move completed actions to logbook” setting is set to “immediately.” However, my Logbook remains completely empty. Sometimes I accidentally swipe right on an action, and now there is no way for me to go back and retrieve that information. This has caused me a lot of frustration. For example, I might accidentally swipe on a grocery list, but then I can’t remember everything I put on it. I have ADHD and this app has been life-changing for me, but its overall utility for me is significantly hurt if I can’t keep a past record or retrieve actions marked completed by accident. I’m considering switching back to a traditional planner rather than renewing my subscription even though it’s much more of a hassle because at least I know my logs can’t be accidentally deleted from a piece of paper

reviews.title: It’s amazing - I could not live my life without it ❤️
reviews.text:
I LOVE this app! It beats the Apple Reminders app by 100%. I’m the type of person that needs to be reminded constantly of what I need to do and needs structure so this has helped me immensely.

Feedback for product:

Sometimes I set reminder to reminder me of something on a certain date or time.

For example, “Make preparations for your appointment tomorrow at 9:00 AM” but the app will literally change the date to tomorrow at 9:00 AM when I want the reminder to be set today at 10:45 PM.

This creates a poor user experience. Luckily, I’m bilingual so I can easily add this reminder in a different language, but I really wish there was a way to toggle this off.

reviews.title: Bug fixes made this app worse
reviews.text: I used to love this app but after a couple rounds of “bug fixes” and updates it isn’t as easy to use as it used to be. You have to be VERY precise when you’re moving a task up or down on your list, otherwise it will try to move that task to another list or it won’t let you place it where you had intended because the area on your screen to which you can grab or drop your task is much smaller than it used to be. Scrolling while grabbing a task isn’t as smooth as it used to be so now I have to grab a task, scroll a little bit, drop it, grab again, scroll, drop it…repeat until the task is in the right location. This app used to make my life easier and now it’s frustrating to use every time. It’s also frustrating that I’m paying for it at this point. Please fix the scrolling and dropping back to what it used to be!!

reviews.title: Please let me run the iPad version on M1 Mac!
reviews.text:
Edit: as I’ve used this app, I’ve noticed more things breaking with each update. As of this update, Home Screen widgets no longer work if I’m in list mode. You used to be able to select just one list to display per widget, but now it makes you choose two… and doesn’t display either of them. 

This app is basically perfect! An absolute delight to use, and has support for home screen widgets *and* standby mode. Fantastic… except why not let us run the iPad version on M1 Macs like a lot of other apps? It’s a simple checkbox on App Store Connect and I could totally put up with the slight iPadOS carry over weirdnesses… I just would love to be able to work on my lists on my Mac for productivity! Please please please consider ticking the checkbox!
